title: Work & colleagues
goal: Chat with colleagues, talk about meetings and deadlines, ask your boss for leave, write a short formal message, understand official announcements and get through a job interview.
intro:
Office Gujarati is a mix: the small talk is relaxed (**ચાલ, ચા પીવા જઈએ**), the nouns are mostly English (**મીટિંગ, ડેડલાઇન, રિપોર્ટ, ઈમેલ**), and the moment you speak to the boss, write a leave application or read a notice, the language turns formal: **આપ**, **જાણ કરશો**, **રજા આપવા વિનંતી**, **નિર્ણય લેવામાં આવ્યો છે**.

This unit teaches both sides. The first grammar point puts the whole **formal register** together (આપ, the polite future as 'please', formal vocabulary, the frame of a letter); the second shows how Gujarati says **'it was decided', 'it has been approved'** — the passive and impersonal forms you hear in every office and read in every notice.

grammar.title: Formal Gujarati: talking up and writing officially
grammar.body:
You already know the three 'you's (Unit 1) and the politeness ladder for requests (Unit 18). At work you need the top of that ladder, consistently.

**Address**: colleagues are first name + **ભાઈ / બેન** (રાજેશભાઈ, હેતલબેન) with **તમે**; the boss is **સર**, **મૅડમ** or surname + **સાહેબ** (મહેતા સાહેબ); very formal speech and writing use **આપ**. Seniors are talked *about* in the plural too: **સાહેબ આવી ગયા**, **મૅડમ મીટિંગમાં છે**.

**Asking**: don't say મારે રજા જોઈએ છે to a boss; ask whether it's possible: **રજા મળી શકે?**, **વાત થઈ શકે?** The **future with આપ / તમે** works as a very polite 'please', in speech and especially in writing: **જોઈ લેશો?** 'would you take a look?', **જાણ કરશો** 'please let me know'. In applications, verb + **-વા વિનંતી** 'request to…' ends the sentence: **રજા આપવા વિનંતી** 'I request leave'.

**Formal words** you'll meet in letters and notices: **જાણ કરવી** (= કહેવું), **ઉપલબ્ધ** (= ફ્રી), **નિર્ણય** (= નક્કી કરેલું), **…ન હોવાથી** 'as … is not' (= કારણ કે … નથી).

**A letter or leave application**: **આદરણીય સર,** → the request → **આભાર.** → **આપનો વિશ્વાસુ,** + your name. (Most office emails are in English; this frame is for applications, schools, banks and government offices.)

The trap: once you start with **આપ**, every verb must be plural: આપ **આવશો**, આપ **છો** — never ~~આપ આવશે~~. And don't slip into **તું** or **યાર** with a boss, however friendly they are.

grammar.title: The passive: 'it was decided', 'the meeting got cancelled'
grammar.body:
English says 'the meeting was cancelled', 'it has been approved'. Gujarati has three ways to leave out who did it, from casual to official.

**1. Everyday: the thing + થવું / થઈ જવું.** This is what you'll say most: **મીટિંગ કૅન્સલ થઈ ગઈ** 'the meeting got cancelled', **કામ થઈ જશે** 'it'll get done', **અરજી મંજૂર થઈ** 'the application was approved'. The verb agrees with the thing (મીટિંગ f → ગઈ).

**2. Formal: verb + -વામાં આવવું.** Take the -વા form and add **માં આવવું**: લેવું → **લેવામાં આવ્યો**, કરવું → **કરવામાં આવી**. **આવવું** carries the tense and agrees with the thing: નિર્ણય (m) **લેવામાં આવ્યો**, રજા (f) મંજૂર **કરવામાં આવી**, and with a કે-clause it goes neuter: **એવું નક્કી કરવામાં આવ્યું કે…** 'it was decided that…'. This is the language of notices, news and HR emails; if you need to name the doer, use **દ્વારા** 'by': **કંપની દ્વારા**.

**3. 'One can / one shouldn't': the -આ- passive.** Add **-આ-** to the stem: બોલ → **બોલાય**, પહેર → **પહેરાય**, ખા → **ખવાય**, પી → **પીવાય**. In the present it means 'one does / one can': **અહીં ગુજરાતી બોલાય છે** 'Gujarati is spoken here', and with **ના** it's the classic way to say 'you're not supposed to': **ઑફિસમાં આવું ના બોલાય** 'you can't say that in the office'.

The trap: don't use the formal -વામાં આવવું for chat with friends — **મીટિંગ કૅન્સલ કરવામાં આવી** sounds like a press release. Say **મીટિંગ કૅન્સલ થઈ ગઈ**.

culture: Gujarati workplaces run on **ભાઈ** and **બેન**: colleagues of any age are Rajeshbhai and Hetalben, which is friendly and respectful at once, while the boss is **સર**, **મૅડમ** or **મહેતા સાહેબ**. Much of Gujarat's economy is still family business — the diamond-polishing units and textile markets of Surat, the trading firms (**પેઢી**) of Ahmedabad's old city — where the owner is the **શેઠ**, deals are sealed over tea, and a good relationship counts for as much as a contract. In IT parks and banks the language of work is Gujlish: English nouns (મીટિંગ, ડેડલાઇન, ક્લાયન્ટ) with Gujarati verbs and politeness. Emails are in English, but leave applications at schools and government offices, bank letters and official notices are in formal Gujarati, full of **જાણ**, **વિનંતી** and **-વામાં આવે છે**. In interviews, especially with older managers, expect personal questions (**ગામ કયું?** 'which is your home town?', family, marriage plans) — they're not considered rude. Across the diaspora, from the motels of the American South to the corner shops of Leicester and Wembley, Gujarati family businesses keep the same mix: Gujarati at the till with the family, English with customers.

lessons.title: Chatting with colleagues

tip.title: Who you call what at work
tip.body:
- Colleagues: first name + **ભાઈ / બેન** (રાજેશભાઈ, હેતલબેન) with **તમે**.
- The boss: **સર**, **મૅડમ** or surname + **સાહેબ**; the owner of a shop or family firm is the **શેઠ**.
- Seniors take a plural verb even when you talk *about* them: **બૉસ આવી ગયા**.
- Save **તું** for close colleagues your own age.

tip.title: By Friday, done and dusted
tip.body:
- 'By' a time is **સુધીમાં**: **શુક્રવાર સુધીમાં** 'by Friday'. Plain **સુધી** means 'until'.
- 'It'll get done': **થઈ જશે**. 'I'll get it done': **પતાવી દઈશ**.
- **દેવું** after a verb means 'done, finished': મોકલી **દીધો**, કરી **દીધું**.
- **ચેક કરીને કહું છું** — 'I'll check and get back to you', the office's favourite line.

lessons.title: Asking the boss, writing formally

tip.title: Formal Gujarati: આપ, -શો, …વા વિનંતી
tip.body:
- Bosses and officials: **તમે / આપ** + plural verb, plus **સર, મૅડમ, સાહેબ**.
- Ask, don't announce: **રજા મળી શકે?** The future is a polite 'please': **જાણ કરશો**.
- Formal words: **જાણ કરવી** (= કહેવું), **ઉપલબ્ધ** (= ફ્રી); applications end with **…વા વિનંતી**.
- After **આપ** the verb is always plural: આપ **છો**, never ~~આપ છે~~.

lessons.title: What was decided

tip.title: The passive: થઈ ગયું, -વામાં આવ્યું, ના બોલાય
tip.body:
- Everyday: the thing + **થઈ જવું** — મીટિંગ કૅન્સલ **થઈ ગઈ**.
- Formal (notices, HR): **-વામાં આવવું** — નિર્ણય **લેવામાં આવ્યો**, રજા મંજૂર **કરવામાં આવી**. **આવવું** agrees with the thing.
- 'You're not supposed to': **-આય** — આવું **ના બોલાય**.
- Name the doer with **દ્વારા** (formal).

lessons.title: Interviews and changing jobs

tip.title: In the interview
tip.body:
- Interviewers use **તમે**; answer with **હા, સર** / **જી**, never યાર.
- 'Tell us about yourself': **તમારા વિશે કંઈક કહો**.
- Experience is 'of years': **મને ત્રણ વર્ષનો અનુભવ છે**.
- Joining is **X માં જોડાવું**; resigning is **રાજીનામું આપવું**.
